summary: NSLAPR argues that E‑Rate should continue to support library special construction, be evaluated on total cost, avoid a national per‑foot cap, raise the Category Two discount to 90 % for high‑discount applicants, and that network‑level filtering already protects patron devices, so software requirements should be dropped and screen‑time decisions left to local boards. Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records (NSLAPR) urges the FCC to keep the E‑Rate program active for libraries and to implement reasonable oversight of consultants to prevent double‑paying or ineligible services. Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records (NSLAPR) argues that special construction should remain eligible, opposes a national per‑foot cap, requests a standing rule for additional extensions, and supports disclosure of state/tribal match and BEAD coordination. Nevada State Library, Archives and Public Records (NSLAPR) argues that existing library filtering practices already protect patrons, that a blanket network‑level filtering rule would impose unnecessary cost and technical burden, and that screen‑time limits should remain under local control.
